claims.claim: The rami CLI supports product search, unit-price sorting, previous orders, live cart listing, and add, update, and remove cart operations.
claims.raw_snippet: Search products, compare unit prices, inspect previous orders, and manage the live Rami Levy cart from a terminal.

claims.claim: Every cart command starts from the latest server cart, while mutations fetch, write, refetch, and verify the complete cart.
claims.raw_snippet: The server is the cart authority. The CLI has no cart cache or snapshot. Every cart command fetches the latest server cart first.

claims.claim: Browser login uses a temporary Chrome profile, captures reduced authentication values, validates them read-only, and deletes the temporary profile without receiving the shopper's password.
claims.raw_snippet: Login uses a new temporary Chrome profile. Request observation starts only after the user presses Enter, so password and OTP submission happen first.

claims.claim: Current-cart promotions affect search sorting only when server-applied, and unit-price comparisons depend on product metadata that may be missing or incorrect.
claims.raw_snippet: Offers are conditional and affect sorting only when the server-calculated current cart includes a discount. Unit prices use Rami Levy content metadata, which can be missing or wrong; do not trust them blindly.

claims.claim: The rami CLI is an MIT-licensed unofficial community project that is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Rami Levy.
claims.raw_snippet: This is an unofficial community project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Rami Levy.
